questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's practical understanding of security and governance gating for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). It tests knowledge of:

- Terraform IaC fundamentals and best practices
- Static analysis security scanning with tfsec
- Custom linting rules with tflint
- GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline configuration
- Secrets management best practices in CI environments

## Key Concepts

**tfsec**: A static analysis security scanner for Terraform code that detects hard-coded credentials, insecure configurations, and common infrastructure vulnerabilities before deployment. It scans for secrets embedded in code and flags misconfigurations that could lead to security breaches.

**tflint**: A extensible linter for Terraform that enforces organization-specific policies. It can be configured with custom rules to ensure consistency across infrastructure code, such as requiring standardized tags on all resources for billing, ownership tracking, and environment classification.

## What Success Looks Like

A strong answer demonstrates:
- Understanding of how tfsec catches secrets at scan time
- Knowledge of tflint's rule configuration for tag enforcement
- Familiarity with GitHub Secrets integration in CI/CD
- Ability to write practical, working Terraform configurations
- Awareness of local vs. CI validation workflows

This combination of skills is essential for maintaining secure, compliant infrastructure at scale.

## Why This Is Asked
Assess practical use of OPA in Kubernetes, translating security expectations into verifiable policies; tests demonstrate understanding of Pod spec structure.

## Key Concepts
- Rego fundamentals
- PodSpec fields: volumes.hostPath, securityContext.privileged, capabilities
- OPA test framework and unit tests
- Admission testing approaches

## Code Example
```javascript
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  some vol in input.request.object.spec.volumes
  vol.hostPath
  msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  c.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "privileged containers are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  some cap in c.securityContext.capabilities.add
  cap == "NET_ADMIN"
  msg := "NET_ADMIN capability is forbidden"
}
```

## Compliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: false
      capabilities:
        add: []
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

## Noncompliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
      capabilities:
        add: ["NET_ADMIN"]
  volumes:
  - name: host-root
    hostPath:
      path: /
```

## Validation Plan
1. Test policy with OPA: `opa test -v policy.rego`
2. Validate compliant pod: `kubectl apply -f compliant.yaml`
3. Verify noncompliant rejection: `kubectl apply -f noncompliant.yaml --dry-run=server`

## Why This Is Asked

Tests a candidate's ability to enforce governance rules on Kubernetes manifests via CI, start with beginner checks, and wire local + CI verification.

## Key Concepts

- PodDisruptionBudget basics
- Pod security via readOnlyRootFilesystem
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- local kubectl dry-run validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# failing manifest (no PDB, readOnlyRootFilesystem: false)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app-a:latest
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# passing manifest (PDB + readOnlyRootFilesystem: true)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app-a@sha256:abc
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb-svc-a
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: svc-a
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (minimal)
name: PDB + ReadOnlyRootFilesystem gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  ck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - name: Lint manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          echo 'Lint step placeholder for yamllint/jsonlint'
      - name: Validate PDB and readOnlyRootFilesystem
        run: |
          # simple validation example
          if ! kubectl get pdb pdb-svc-a >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'PDB missing for svc-a'; exit 1
          fi
          if ! grep -R "readOnlyRootFilesystem: true" -n k8s || true; then
            echo 'Some container not enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem'; exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to cover all namespaces and workloads beyond Deployments? 
- What are the trade-offs of enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem strictly vs allowing certain privileged ops for debugging?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world expertise in supply chain security by testing the ability to tie SBOMs to runtime admission policies. It aligns with vendor-agnostic security frameworks (SLSA, SBOM) and modern GitOps deployment patterns where provenance verification is critical.

## Key Concepts

- **CycloneDX SBOMs**: Standardized software bills of materials that document container contents
- **Image digests**: SHA256 references ensuring immutable image pinning
- **Kyverno admission control**: Policy engine validating deployments at Kubernetes admission time
- **Helm chart provenance**: Ensuring charts reference verified, SBOM-backed images

## Proposed Solution

### GitHub Actions Workflow: Generate and Publish SBOMs

```yaml
name: SBOM Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: cyclonedx-json
          image: ${{ github.repository }}
          output-file: sbom.json
      - run: |
          echo "${{ steps.sbom.outputs.sbom-json }}" | ghcr.io/your-org/sbom-store:latest 
            --image=${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
```

### Kyverno Policy: Enforce SBOM Presence at Admission

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: validate-sbom-present
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        - Deployment
        - StatefulSet
        - DaemonSet
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ request.operation }}"
        operator: In
        value: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    validate:
      message: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: ""
          - key: "{{ lookup('sbom.verify', '{{ element.image }}', 'cyclonedx') }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: "valid"
```

### Failing Manifest (No SBOM)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vulnerable-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vulnerable-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vulnerable-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment blocked with error: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"

### Passing Manifest (SBOM Verified)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: verified-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: verified-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: verified-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/app@sha256:a1b2c3d4e5f6...
        annotations:
          sbom.cyclonedx: "ghcr.io/your-org/app/sbom/a1b2c3d4e5f6"
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment allowed

## Testing Steps

1. **Apply Kyverno policy**: `kubectl apply -f kyverno-policy.yaml`
2. **Test failing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-no-sbom.yaml` — should be rejected
3. **Test passing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-with-sbom.yaml` — should be admitted
4. **Verify SBOM storage**: Confirm SBOMs are queryable via your SBOM service endpoint
5. **Audit logs**: Check Kyverno policy reports for enforcement details

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
```

- How would you extend to multi-container pods?
- How would you adapt for multiple charts in a single repo?
